主要内容: Chesapeake Energy, a pioneer in the U.S. shale revolution, filed for bankruptcy protection on June 28, 2020. The move comes amid a drop in oil and gas prices due to the coronavirus pandemic. The company said that $7 billion in debt will be wiped out through the restructuring. Chesapeake has secured $925 million in debtor-in-possession financing to continue operations during the bankruptcy process. Additionally, the company has secured an agreement in principle for $2.5 billion in debt financing and a backstop commitment for $600 million in new equity. Franklin Resources and Fidelity are among the biggest creditors and will be primary equity holders post-restructuring. The company will continue operations at a reduced capacity with a handful of gas rigs and no oil rigs. CEO Doug Lawler stated that the restructuring aims to address legacy financial weaknesses and capitalize on operational strengths. Chesapeake was founded in 1989 by Aubrey McClendon, who was ousted in 2013 and later died in a car crash in 2016. The company's debt was nearly as high as Exxon and Chevron combined when Lawler took over. The downturn is not unique, as other companies like Whiting Petroleum also filed for bankruptcy protection.
